svg.title: Four Checks Before Dispatch or Scope Expansion
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-preflight-statutory-risk-checks; chart type: decision_tree; title: Four Checks Before Dispatch or Scope Expansion; subtitle: Proceed only through applicable, documented operating requirements.; chapter number: 5; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Numbers identify sequential decisions rather than risk scores. A failed check routes to the corrective action in its detail. Texas citations are jurisdiction-specific examples, not nationwide contractor rules.; caption: Coverage uncertainty does not authorize contractor claim negotiation, deductible concessions, or unsafe mobilization.; stages: label: Credentials match the work?; value: Yes: continue; no: reassign scope; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Verify local contractor requirements and applicable remediation licensing, including Texas Occupations Code Chapter 1958 where relevant. If credentials are missing, exclude the work or use a properly qualified provider under a permitted contracting arrangement.; label: Activity stays within contractor scope?; value: Yes: continue; no: redirect request; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Under Texas Insurance Code sections 4102.051 and 4102.163, assess licensing and contractor restrictions before any adjusting activity. Explain construction quantities and prices; redirect coverage advocacy or settlement negotiation to an authorized professional.; label: Payment terms preserve required deductibles?; value: Yes: continue; no: correct terms; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Review Texas Business and Commerce Code section 27.02 where applicable. Reject prohibited deductible waivers, disguised rebates, and inflated invoices; document the customer's actual payment obligations and collection path.; label: Hazards and cash exposure controlled?; value: Yes: dispatch; no: resolve deficiencies; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Apply 29 CFR 1910.134 when respiratory protection is required, 29 CFR 1926.1101 for covered asbestos work, and 40 CFR 745.85 for covered renovations. Assign qualified crews, protective measures, and funded job commitments before releasing affected work.

rect.title: label: Credentials match the work?; value: Yes: continue; no: reassign scope; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Verify local contractor requirements and applicable remediation licensing, including Texas Occupations Code Chapter 1958 where relevant. If credentials are missing, exclude the work or use a properly qualified provider under a permitted contracting arrangement.
